title: Shell + Skills + Compaction: Tips for long-running agents that do real work
relevance_note: OpenAI engineering post describing in-stream server-side compaction vs explicit compaction calls, plus on-demand loading of 'skills' to reduce prompt bloat.
reason_included: Concrete harness-level mechanisms for compiling context on demand (skills) and maintaining continuity via compaction and thread continuation.

claim_snippets.claim_text: The post distinguishes server-side compaction (automatic, in-stream when context crosses a threshold) from the standalone `/responses/compact` endpoint (explicit control over when compaction happens).

Skills are described as a bundle of files with a `SKILL.md` manifest; when skills are available, the platform exposes each skill’s metadata (`name`, `description`, `path`) to the model, and the model reads `SKILL.md` only if it decides to invoke the skill.
The post claims combining container reuse, passing `previous_response_id`, and using compaction reduces restart behaviour and keeps multi-step jobs coherent as the thread grows.
